items: Former PBA star Peter June 'PJ' Simon passed away at the age of 46 after collapsing during a basketball game.
Simon had a legendary 16-year career with the Purefoods/Magnolia franchise, earning multiple accolades including eight PBA All-Star selections and a Grand Slam title in 2014.
He is remembered for his humility and professionalism, with his jersey No. 8 retired in honor of his contributions to the team and the sport.

MANILA, Philippines – Former PBA star Peter June “PJ” Simon died on Friday, November 20, after collapsing in a basketball game. He was 46.
The Purefoods/Magnolia franchise confirmed his passing in a social media post.

“Isa si PJ sa pinakamagandang ehemplo ng isang professional basketball player (PJ is one of the best examples of a professional basketball player),” the team said. “You competed with quiet confidence, carried yourself with humility, and wore #8 with a pride everyone could feel.”
“You represented the franchise in the best way possible, and that is why you are beloved not just by Hotshots fans, but every Filipino basketball fan.”

Though no official cause of death was given, multiple videos online showed Simon being fanned by teammates on the sideline and eventually carried off-court after an apparent mid-game collapse in what looked like a recreational match in Davao City.

Drafted 43rd overall in 2001, Simon quickly established himself as one of the greatest PBA draft steals, eventually carving out a legendary 16-year career entirely with the Purefoods/Magnolia franchise, and earning the iconic moniker “The Scoring Apostle.”

Forming a feared guard duo with fellow franchise icon and shooter James Yap, Simon provided excellent production mostly off the bench, enough to earn him eight PBA All-Star selections and win Mr. Quality Minutes twice.

Alongside fellow stars like Yap, Marc Pingris, and Mark Barroca, Simon immortalized himself in PBA lore in 2014 after helping Purefoods — named the San Mig Coffee Mixers at the time — win the ultimate PBA title trifecta, the rare Grand Slam, under head coach Tim Cone.
“This is so sudden, Part. I didn’t expect it at all,” Yap wrote in Bisaya in a social media post.
“Thank you for everything, Part, for all the times we spent together that I will never forget. We still have a basketball tour to do. This is painful, Part.”

In 2019, Magnolia handed Simon the rare honor of retiring his iconic jersey No. 8, after the Cotabato native helped the franchise win eight PBA titles with averages of 10.1 points in under 22 minutes across nearly 700 games.

After the 2001 PBA draft, Simon started to make a name for himself in the defunct Metropolitan Basketball Association and the Philippine Basketball League, becoming a two-time PBL champion and one-time MVP, before finally suiting up for Purefoods in 2004.

After retiring from the PBA in 2020, Simon made a brief return to the pro ranks in 2024 with the Davao Occidental Tigers of the Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League before again hanging up his sneakers a year later.

“We’ll always remember the eight championships and the Grand Slam. We’ll miss that signature one-hander from midrange. We’ll always think of the clutch shots and heat checks of ‘The Scoring Apostle,'” the Purefoods/Magnolia franchise said.
“Most of all, we’ll miss the person we got to share those moments with.”
Simon is survived by his wife, Jehza, and two children. – Rappler.com
